clue.text: Rebekeh's first affair getting considerable coverage

definitions.text: Rebekeh's first affair getting considerable coverage
definitions.note: the whole clue points at the media owner whose papers Rebekah Brooks ran

indicators.note: getting coverage means being wrapped up inside something else, so the earlier pieces sit within the next word

parts.note: much means a considerable amount

indicators.note: the first of a name is its opening letter, so only the initial of Rebekeh is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
a do is a party or social affair

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about Rebekah Brooks's early love life getting wall-to-wall press.
explanation.walkthrough: This anniversary puzzle brings in names that Private Eye clues have used for years and gives them only loose definitions. Rebekah Brooks ran newspapers for Rupert Murdoch, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch owns newspapers, and Rebekah Brooks, once his editor and favourite, was his paper's chief, so press coverage is his business.

clue.text: State of the country: close to downfall and collapse ultimately

parts.note: for a British setter the country is the United Kingdom
rain is a downfall from the sky

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of collapse is used

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A report on the state of the nation, warning that it is near ruin and will finally fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like part of the gloom, but here it just means the next piece sits beside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a sovereign country in eastern Europe, and state is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: State "Not elected"

definitions.note: the whole clue: a figure of state whom nobody voted for

indicators.note: not marks what follows as missing, so that word's letters are taken out of the state's name

parts.note: Indiana is a US state
a politician who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A two-word verdict on a candidate: the state has declared them unelected.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana is one of the themed names. A royal is a figure of state whom nobody elected, so the whole clue describes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Princess of Wales, held a public royal role by marriage, never by any vote.

clue.text: Belittled Conservative draped round dressing material

definitions.text: Belittled Conservative draped round dressing material
definitions.note: the whole clue loosely evokes a disgraced politician

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative, the word cut down

explanation.surface: A humiliated politician wrapped in bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Clinton is one of the themed names, defined only loosely; he was belittled by scandal, though not a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton, the former US President, was humiliated by the Lewinsky scandal, which the whole clue loosely evokes.

clue.text: Bill's back from holiday venue

definitions.note: the whole clue loosely names the politician as wordplay only

explanation.walkthrough: John Major, Conservative Prime Minister in the 1990s, is one of the themed names, given only the wordplay as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major, the former British Prime Minister, is a themed name the setter defines only through this wordplay.

clue.text: Divine gift, hogging the party

definitions.note: the whole clue: a divine star who steals the show

parts.note: manna is the food God sent the Israelites in the desert

explanation.walkthrough: Madonna, the singer, is one of the themed names; her name means the Virgin Mary, hence 'Divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is a pop diva whose name is the title of the Virgin Mary, and who famously hogs the limelight.

clue.text: President 4's second Monica, so it's said

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Thomas ..., third President of the United States
second meaning: the middle name of 4 down, with Monica standing for its sound-alike moniker

explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is Clinton, whose full name is William Jefferson Clinton. Monica, said aloud, is moniker, a name, and Monica Lewinsky is also the scandal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Jefferson led the US, and Jefferson is also Bill Clinton's middle name, his second moniker.

clue.text: About Cameron's lead: finished — get over it!

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A heckler telling David Cameron's party that its leader's time is up and to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover from something is to get past it, the same idea as getting over a shock or loss.

clue.text: Screwed Monica's head off — Republican grandee starts to break it up, which is natural

indicators.note: breaking it up means pushing into the middle of it, so the new letters go inside the rearranged ones
something screwed is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
with its head off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: the name as written

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one from each

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of Monica Lewinsky being bedded, with an elder Republican stepping in to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed' reads as sexual slang in the surface; here it means twisted. The rearranged letters are split after their first letter to take the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food is grown without chemicals, so organic is used to mean natural or unprocessed.

clue.text: Balls provided, hard stuff gives erection?

parts.note: Ed Balls was a Labour politician, Shadow Chancellor at the time
provided means on condition that, as if does
ice is frozen, hard water

explanation.surface: A crude question: given balls and something hard, do you get an erection?
explanation.walkthrough: Balls is a person here, not body parts. Ed Balls was a senior Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, and in the architect's sense an erection is a structure put up.

clue.text: Britain's in a bad way with state intervention, Coalition style?

indicators.note: an intervention comes between parts, so the state's letters are placed inside the others
a thing in a bad way is in disorder, so its letters are muddled

parts.note: the word as written, without its apostrophe
PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A gloomy comment that the country is in trouble because of government meddling, the coalition way.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain had a Conservative and Liberal Democrat coalition government in 2013. 'State intervention' sounds like government action; here state is just a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisan means backed by two parties together, which is how a coalition government works.

clue.text: Remainder of Right and Left half breaking up in Southern America

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

indicators.note: each half of the pair breaks into the next word, splitting it, so one of its letters sits on each side
being in a region means sitting inside its borders, so everything before goes between the outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
the United States
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political note about what is left of the right and left wings falling apart in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L each take one half of the word up: U then R, P then L. All that sits between S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over after needs are met, so it is a remainder.

clue.text: Resentment when diplomat fails to get round in

indicators.note: failing to get something in means it is left out, so that letter is missing

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent on a mission
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: Bitterness felt by an ambassador who cannot get his round in at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a round in' sounds like buying drinks; here round is the ring-shaped letter, and the final 'in' says where it should have been.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is the resentful wish to have what someone else has, so resentment is a close synonym.

clue.text: Not one to give away what the lawyer pocketed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who retains, holding on to things
second meaning: the advance fee paid to secure a lawyer's services

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark reads like a remark about a greedy lawyer; it signals that the first meaning is a made-up word, 'one who retains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a fee paid in advance to keep a barrister or solicitor available, and literally one who keeps hold.

clue.text: Army hit with a battering involving hydrogen — ticker malfunction

indicators.note: involving means including, so the element's symbol joins the other letters
a battering knocks things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Soldiers hit hard in a hydrogen bomb attack, leaving someone with heart trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticker is slang for the heart. This spelling with one R is a variant of ARRHYTHMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrhythmia is an irregular heartbeat, a fault in the heart's rhythm, and ticker is slang for heart.

clue.text: Muscles crap? Time out, stupid!

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: a crude word for a lump of excrement
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gym-goer told that their muscles are rubbish and to call time out on the silliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd means ridiculous or senseless, so it can stand for stupid as an adjective.

clue.text: Protestor's married off?

clue.text: Luvvie-style prattle, which is often forced

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word extras mutter on stage to sound like a crowd talking
second meaning: the plant whose stalks are grown early in the dark

explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a showy theatre type. Forced rhubarb is grown in the dark to bring it on early, a speciality of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors mumble the word as background noise, so it means nonsense talk, and the plant is commonly forced for early stalks.

clue.text: 21's crowning glory: orchestrating the absolute end of Keir Hardie?

indicators.note: orchestrating means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order
the absolute end of a word is its very last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning the final end of Keir Hardie, the Labour Party's founder.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is Neil Kinnock, Labour leader in the 1980s, known for his ginger hair. Keir Hardie founded the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's crowning glory is their hair, and Kinnock's was famously ginger.

clue.text: Sylvan creature has desire to grab balls on date

two round O letters look like balls

explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the balls above the date, so those two pieces travel together inside the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvan means of the woods, and a wood ant is an ant that lives in forests.

clue.text: Elected to penetrate slag

clue.text: Great capacity for wine, this arsehole
